text:
Ops Oncall: FYI alert from eu-west fleet — after rolling NCCL 2.19 to the inference pool we’re seeing intermittent collective timeouts that stall multi-GPU inference jobs
Maria: seeing the same in staging yesterday morning, briefly hit 100% of queued requests on p4d-cluster-12
Kevin: can you paste the alert log?
Ops Oncall: paste below — truncated: 
```
ALERT: collective_timeout on gpu-node-23
service: inference-runtime
model: llama-13b
error: NCCL AllReduce timeout after 120s
stack: libnccl.so.2.19 -> nv_peer_memory -> rdma_cm_connect timeout
metrics: increased allreduce_wait_time, KV cache hits stable
```
Maria: dmesg on one of the impacted nodes shows repeated `mlx5_core` link flaps around the same time, but not all nodes show it.
Sara: interesting — we rolled both NCCL 2.19 and CUDA driver 535.86 at the same time on eu-west. Could be driver/kernel mismatch with mlx5 firmware.
Jordan: logs from the nv_peer_memory module show "rdma_connect failed: -110" a lot. Does this match RDMA/SGX NIC firmware?
Kevin: I'm collecting per-node NCCL logs. Quick grep for ERROR:
```
$ grep -i "ERROR\|timeout" /var/log/nccl/*.log | tail -n 50
gpu-node-23: [0] NCCL ERROR Call to op failed : unhandled system error (unreachable)
gpu-node-34: [1] NCCL Timeout waiting for op
gpu-node-12: [2] nv_peer_memory: device reset triggered
```
Maria: also noticed CPU steal high on some nodes from noisy neighbor k8s daemons during collectives — might exacerbate stalls for synchronous allreduce.
Ops Oncall: infra-bot reports we rolled 2.19 to 80% of eu-west on 1778499800 via canary job `nccl-upgrade-eu-west`.
infra-bot: deployment `nccl-upgrade-eu-west` completed: 80% -> paused (manual stop) at 1778499800 by deploy-scheduler
Sara: propose immediate partial rollback of the canary to 2.18 for the most-affected instance groups (p4d-ws-*, p4d-burst-*) and open a deeper RCA ticket. Who can own the rollback?
Kevin: I can patch and run rollback for the p4d-ws auto-scaling group now. Will annotate the change in the deploy.
Jordan: while Kevin does that, let's enable increased NCCL logging and async error handling on a subset to gather better traces: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ens5
Maria: also recommend setting UCX_LOG_LEVEL=info on those pods and capture `ibv_devinfo` + `rdma_cm` counters.
Kevin: rolling rollback for target group p4d-ws-1..3 -> downgrading libnccl2 to 2.18.4, driver stays for now.
(10m later) Kevin: rollback applied to p4d-ws-1..3. Monitoring shows queued request count dropping, tail latency improving.
Ops Oncall: alert rate dropped ~70% for that ASG. Good catch.
Sara: next steps: reproduce in an isolated test harness with NCCL 2.19 + driver 535.86 against same kernel (5.15.0) and mlx5 firmware. If we can reproduce, file bug with vendor (Mellanox/NVIDIA).
Jordan: suggestion: run a synthetic allreduce benchmark with nccl-tests (all_reduce_perf) across the same AZ and collect ib stats:
```
./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 2048 -g 8 -c 0
# run pinned to same cpu set and capture `perf top` and `dmesg -w`
```
Maria: we should avoid wide rollout until RCA. Also document the cost impact — stalled jobs consumed burst GPUs for extra hours yesterday; Finance wants a short note.
Kevin: summarizing action items I took: rollback p4d-ws-1..3 -> 2.18.4, captured NCCL logs (uploaded to /mnt/logs/nccl/1778501234), enabled NCCL_DEBUG on diag group.
Jordan: I’ll set up the test harness and run nccl-tests with and without nv_peer_memory and with different RDMA providers (verbs vs gdr_copy).
Sara: if firmware mismatch suspected, coordinate with cloud provider to check mlx5 firmware and NIC driver (mlx5_core) patch levels.
Ops Oncall: reopening the canary is blocked until we confirm fix. tagging support/sre on this thread.
Maria: FYI — a few customers on Dedicated noticed degraded throughput; CS pinged me. I'll send a customer-facing note after we have root cause. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ticket created INC-2026-3412 "NCCL 2.19 collectives timeouts in eu-west" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1
Kevin: will follow up with detailed logs + perf numbers in the ticket. For now, keeping 2.19 paused in eu-west.
Jordan: plan for next 24h: repro, capture rdma/ib counters, try nv_peer_memory off, test with CUDA driver 534.x fallback if needed.
Sara: great. If anyone finds a quick mitigation that keeps canary running safely (e.g., switching to single-GPU inference routing for certain models), propose it here and we can flip routing in the router service.
Ops Oncall: thanks all — I'll update the incident channel and set pager rotation.
Kevin: one more note — we saw one node where setting `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` prevented the hang in our stress test. Not a fix but useful signal about cross-node p2p paths.
Maria: good data point. Add it to the ticket.
(ended thread)
